pass_a_gloss: Continue the heirs of God question: Levi’s sons get no lot among brothers because the Lord is their portion and inheritance—that sense holds. Glory riches of God’s inheritance arise in saints’ minds able to hold so much God and Word contemplation by surpassing divine power toward saints and believers. Knowing hope of calling and inheritance glory needs not ordinary power but greatness of power entering believers from him, by the working of all ruling strength Paul names might of his strength—the same working that raised Christ from the dead. Seated at the right above every rule, authority, power, lordship, and named name in this age and the next; all under his feet; head over all to the church his body, fullness of the one who fills all in all: take this as figure, not literal heavenly chairs for Father and Son at the Father’s right. Earth is not a bodily footstool under a seated God either; Isaiah’s span measured heaven and handful held earth forbid that reading. Nearness and distance to God are intelligible matters: saints living by the Father of all’s will draw near, while the ungodly put themselves far and perish, as the prophet warns. So saints are said to be at his right and the ungodly as it were at his left, matching the Savior’s sheep on the right and goats on the left. “Seated at the right” means established with gifted kingship and rule by which Jesus oversees the saints, benefiting them and sharing himself—set above all through philanthropic stewardship toward everything. Many rulers, authorities, lordships, and power sharers work in this age or will work in the next, yet none rules a rule as great as the Son’s. All that rule need him as their ruler; authorities will rule better under Christ’s authority because God’s power excels every other; even when good lordships lead others into useful service, they must take the craft of lording from the Lord of those who lord. Hence the one who raised Christ seated him above every rule and authority and power and lordship and every name named not only now but also later—including names unutterable and indescribable in the whole arrangement, some for this age and some for the next. Those names came to the apostle from the revealing Holy Spirit. How “he subjected all things under his feet” is said needs scrutiny while myriads still refuse the Word of God; we do not yet see all subjected, and “he must reign until he puts all enemies under his feet” shows enemies are not yet all underfoot. pass_b_english: also understand the heirs of God. And the law that says, “But the sons of Levi shall not be given a lot among their brothers, because I am their portion, says the Lord,” and elsewhere, “the Lord is their inheritance,” holds to such a sense. So the riches of the glory of God’s inheritance come to be in the mind of the saints who will contain so much of the contemplation of God and of his Word by the surpassing greatness of God’s power toward the saints and believers. For it is not ordinary power from God that we need in order to know what is the hope of his calling and what the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints, but a greatness of his power coming to be in us who believe from him, and coming according to the working of his strength that rules all things, which Paul now names “might of his strength”; and using this working of the might of his strength he worked what he worked in Christ when he raised him from the dead.

Ephesians 1:20–23: “and seated him at his right hand in the heavenly places above every rule and authority and power and lordship and every name that is named, not only in this age but also in the one to come; and he subjected all things under his feet, and gave him as head over all things to the church, which is his body, the fullness of him who fills all in all.” These things must be taken in a bodily figure, not as if certain seats or sense-perceptible thrones lie in the heavens on which the Father sits and the Son at the Father’s right; for thinking that way we would not say these things worthily of the divine nature. Nor is the earth bodily subject to God himself as a footstool under his feet when he sits in heaven. For how can heaven be a throne, measured by his span? And the earth a footstool of his feet, itself also enclosed in his hand? For Isaiah says, “Who measured the water with his hand and the heaven with a span and all the earth with a handful?” I think, then, that being near God and far from him are intelligible: all the saints who live according to the will of the Father of all and draw near to God, while the ungodly are far from him, of whom the prophet says, “Behold, those who put themselves far from you will perish.” As, then, one has understood who is near God and who is far from him, so one must take the saints as said to be at his right and the ungodly as it were at his left, just as the Savior also says he sets the sheep on the right and the goats on the left. And “having seated at the right” is such as this: “having established and gifted him kingship and rule,” according to which he oversees and rules the saints, benefiting them and sharing himself—Jesus who became above all through the philanthropic stewardship toward all.

Many, then, are the things that rule and lead those who need oversight from him, and many that hold authority, and many that lord it, and many that share their own power—some in this age, some also to work in the age to come; yet none of these rules a rule as great as the Son. For all that rule need him as their ruler; and authorities will rule better when under Christ’s authority, God’s power excelling every remaining power; and even if some are led into beneficial slavery by those who lord well, those who lord must take the science of lording from the Lord of those who lord, to lord over what they lord. Hence the one who raised Christ from the dead seated him at his right in the heavenly places, above every rule and authority and power and lordship and every name named not only in this age but also in the one to come; for it is likely there are also unutterable and indescribable names named according to the arrangement of the whole, not graspable by us—some in this age, but also some in the one to come. And from where did the apostle have these names if not from the Holy Spirit that revealed them to him? And how “he subjected all things under his feet” is said must be examined, since it is plain that countless people still refuse to submit to the Word of God.
